products.note: Managed foundation model API service; IAM integration; VPC support; model evaluation tools; AgentCore for agent orchestration

reading.body:
AWS generated $717 billion in revenue through 2025 and offers two primary AI product lines: SageMaker for full machine learning lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model APIs.

The scale of AWS revenue reflects its position as the dominant cloud infrastructure provider globally. Both products sit directly in the compute abstraction layer. SageMaker addresses the full workflow from data ingestion through model deployment and monitoring. Bedrock commodifies access to foundation models themselves, bundling model inference with standard cloud security and orchestration primitives like IAM, VPC, and agent frameworks.

For AI scaling specifically, this matters because neither product appears to address power or physical infrastructure constraints. SageMaker optimizes the software layer above compute. Bedrock abstracts which models run where but does not disclose how AWS has provisioned or will provision the underlying accelerator capacity to serve either product at scale. The data does not show energy efficiency commitments, grid agreements, or datacenter build plans tied to AI demand.

The legal exposure count of 52 records in Washington state indicates regulatory activity, but the data does not identify which concerns apply to AI versus AWS's broader operations, or whether they touch infrastructure, data residency, or other domains material to AI's physical constraints.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc., a public company founded in 1994 and headquartered in Seattle, WA. AWS is a for-profit cloud computing provider listed on public markets under the ticker AMZN. According to SEC filings, Amazon reported revenue of $716,924,000,000 for the period ending December 31, 2025.

AWS's primary AI product tracked on this site is Amazon SageMaker, which the company describes as "the center for all your data, analytics, and AI." The platform is positioned as a unified development environment covering the full machine learning lifecycle, including model training, customization, deployment, monitoring, bias detection, and explainability tools. The next-generation SageMaker Unified Studio brings together model development tools such as HyperPod, JumpStart, and MLOps capabilities alongside generative AI, data processing, and SQL analytics, with Amazon Q Developer serving as an integrated AI assistant for tasks including model building, SQL query generation, and data pipeline creation. The platform supports a lakehouse architecture spanning Amazon S3 data lakes, Amazon Redshift data warehouses, and Apache Iceberg-compatible tools, with federated query access to third-party data sources and zero-ETL integrations for near-real-time data ingestion. AWS also offers AWS Bedrock, a managed foundation model API service that includes IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and an AgentCore component for agent orchestration.

The held facts indicate AWS carries law exposure associated with Washington state, with 55 cases on record in that jurisdiction. No litigation cases, MCP server registrations, or patent filings are recorded in the current data for this entry.
